name: Hallstatt Salzberg & Skywalk
access: Walk up from Hallstatt-Lahn, or ride the Salzbergbahn funicular
access_note: The Soleweg section Salzberg–Steeg is closed after rockfall; check hallstatt.net.
trending_reason: Hallstatt is Europe’s best-known overtourism story; the Skywalk is its classic overhead shot
blurb: A steep zigzag path, or the funicular, to the Skywalk platform 360 m above Hallstatt, with the whole lake and the Dachstein below.
description: Above Hallstatt’s lakeside rooftops a steep path zigzags up through the forest (or ride the Salzbergbahn funicular) to the Welterbeblick Skywalk, a platform jutting out 360 m above the village with the Hallstätter See and the Dachstein massif laid out below. The salt mine up here has been worked for some 7,000 years and can be visited. Come early or late: the village fills with day visitors by mid-morning.

name: Gosausee Lake Loop
access: Car or bus to the Gosausee car park
trending_reason: The Dachstein glacier mirrored in a still lake
blurb: An easy loop round the Vorderer Gosausee, with the Dachstein glacier reflected in the water at its head.
description: An easy, almost level walk round the Vorderer Gosausee, where on a still morning the Dachstein glacier and the jagged Gosaukamm reflect perfectly in the water. About an hour all round; add the walk to the Hinterer Gosausee or the climb to the Holzmeisteralm for a half-day. The lake sits at the end of the Gosau valley road, with a large car park and a bus stop.

name: Dachstein 5fingers Platform
access: Dachstein Krippenstein cable car from Obertraun
trending_reason: A hand-shaped viewing platform hanging over the void above Lake Hallstatt
blurb: From the Krippenstein cable car a short walk leads to five platform “fingers” jutting out over a sheer drop, with Lake Hallstatt far below.
description: From the Krippenstein cable car station above Obertraun, a short walk leads to the 5fingers: five steel platforms shaped like the fingers of a hand, cantilevered over a sheer drop with Lake Hallstatt and the village far below. The same lift serves the Dachstein Giant Ice Cave at its middle station, so the two combine into an easy day.

name: Pasterze Glacier Trail & Gamsgrubenweg
access: Grossglockner High Alpine Road (toll; €41.50 advance car day ticket in 2026)
access_note: The Gamsgrubenweg is closed beyond tunnel 6 except for mountaineers.
trending_reason: Austria’s highest peak above its longest, fast-retreating glacier
blurb: Down to the shrinking Pasterze glacier and back along the tunnelled Gamsgrubenweg, with the Grossglockner (3,798 m) towering above.
description: At the end of the Grossglockner High Alpine Road, the Kaiser-Franz-Josefs-Höhe looks straight at Austria’s highest peak, the Grossglockner (3,798 m), and down onto the Pasterze, the country’s longest glacier and fast retreating. The trail drops towards the ice and returns along the Gamsgrubenweg, a balcony path through six short tunnels where marmots and ibex are common. Beyond tunnel 6 the path is for mountaineers only.

name: Pinzgauer Spaziergang
area: Kitzbühel Alps · Zell am See → Saalbach
access: Schmittenhöhebahn up from Zell am See; Schattberg X-Press down to Saalbach, bus back
trending_reason: Lonely Planet’s pick for Austria’s best high-level day hike
blurb: A long balcony walk along the grassy Kitzbühel Alps with the glaciated Hohe Tauern, Grossglockner included, in view all day.
description: A long, grassy balcony walk from the Schmittenhöhe above Zell am See west along the Kitzbühel Alps towards Saalbach. No hard climbing, just a gently undulating path around and over a string of rounded tops, with the glaciated Hohe Tauern, Grossglockner and Grossvenediger included, across the Salzach valley all day. Ride up the Schmittenhöhebahn, down the Schattberg X-Press to Saalbach, and take the bus back.

name: Krimml Waterfalls Trail
access: Bus or car to Krimml; the trail starts at the lower falls
access_note: Wasserfallweg admission about €9; open mid-April to the end of October.
trending_reason: Austria’s highest waterfall (380 m), a perennial top Austria sight
blurb: A well-built path climbs beside all three tiers of the 380 m falls, with spray-soaked viewpoints at every bend.
description: Austria’s highest waterfall drops 380 m in three tiers in the Hohe Tauern National Park. The Wasserfallweg climbs beside it on well-built switchbacks with viewpoints at every bend; expect to get wet from the spray at the lower falls. Turn back at the upper falls or continue into the quieter Krimmler Achental. The trail charges admission and is open from mid-April to the end of October.

name: Lünersee Loop
access: Lünerseebahn cable car from the end of the Brandnertal
trending_reason: A turquoise high lake under the Schesaplana
blurb: Ride the cable car to the Douglasshütte and circle the turquoise Lünersee at 1,970 m beneath the Schesaplana.
description: A cable car lifts you from the end of the Brandnertal to the Douglasshütte on the shore of the Lünersee, a turquoise lake at 1,970 m beneath the Schesaplana in the Rätikon. The loop round the lake is easy and mostly level, with one short climb on the far side; marmots and wildflowers keep it lively in July. The lake is a dammed reservoir, but you would hardly know.

name: Goetheweg: Hafelekar to Pfeishütte
access: Nordkettenbahnen from Innsbruck city centre to Hafelekar
trending_reason: City centre to summit in about half an hour; the Nordkette is Innsbruck’s signature trip
blurb: From the top of the Nordkette cable cars along the airy Goetheweg into the wild Karwendel to the Pfeishütte, with Innsbruck 1,700 m below.
description: Two cable cars carry you from Innsbruck’s centre to Hafelekar at 2,256 m. From there the Goetheweg traverses the north side of the Nordkette, above the wild Karwendel valleys, to the Pfeishütte: an airy but well-made path with short cabled sections, and the city 1,700 m below at the start. Walk back the same way to the cable car, or descend via the Arzler Alm. Surefootedness required.

name: Schafberg from St. Wolfgang
access: Start in St. Wolfgang; the Schafbergbahn cog railway can replace the climb or the descent
trending_reason: Wolfgangsee, Mondsee and Attersee in one view from the summit hotel
blurb: A big climb from the lakeshore at St. Wolfgang to the summit hotel above Wolfgangsee, Mondsee and Attersee, or ride the historic cog railway one way.
description: A big day from the lakeshore at St. Wolfgang to the 1,783 m summit of the Schafberg, where the hotel terrace looks down on three lakes at once: Wolfgangsee, Mondsee and Attersee. The climb is long and steep in places but not technical. The historic Schafbergbahn cog railway runs all the way up, so you can walk one way and ride the other.

name: Grüner See Loop
access: Paid car park at the lake (€6/day); bus 175 from Bruck an der Mur
access_note: Best mid-May to June; the lake shrinks through the summer.
trending_reason: Spring snowmelt floods the park; the underwater benches and paths went viral
blurb: An easy loop round a crystal-clear lake under the Hochschwab that swells with snowmelt each spring, flooding the park paths beneath it.
description: In spring, snowmelt from the Hochschwab fills the Grüner See at Tragöß until it floods the park around it: benches, bridges and paths end up metres under crystal-clear water. The easy loop round the lake is best from mid-May to June; by late summer it shrinks back to a small pond. Paid car park at the lake, or the bus from Bruck an der Mur.

name: Lechweg
access: Summer bus from Lech to the Formarinsee
trending_reason: A headline long-distance route in 2026 tour programmes, along one of the last wild rivers in the Alps
blurb: Follow the Lech from its source lake to the Lechfall at Füssen: gravel banks, suspension bridges and valley villages, mostly downhill.
description: A long-distance walk along one of the last wild rivers in the northern Alps, from the Formarinsee near the Lech’s source in Vorarlberg, down the Lechtal to the Lechfall at Füssen in Bavaria. Mostly downhill after the first stage, it follows gravel banks, suspension bridges and valley villages, with daily stages of roughly 15–20 km: an approachable first multi-day hike.

name: Eagle Walk (Adlerweg)
area: St. Johann in Tirol → St. Christoph am Arlberg
access: Train to St. Johann in Tirol
trending_reason: Tyrol’s flagship long-distance trail, 33 stages across the whole province
blurb: Tyrol’s long-distance trail from the Wilder Kaiser across the Karwendel and Lechtal Alps to the Arlberg: 24 North Tyrol stages plus a 9-stage East Tyrol branch.
description: Tyrol’s flagship long-distance trail, named for the eagle shape it draws across the map. The main line runs 24 stages from St. Johann in Tirol over the Wilder Kaiser, the Karwendel and the Lechtal Alps to St. Christoph am Arlberg; a separate 9-stage East Tyrol branch crosses the Hohe Tauern between the Grossvenediger and the Grossglockner. Stages run hut to hut or valley to valley and are easily done in sections.

name: Stubai High Trail (Stubaier Höhenweg)
access: Bus from Innsbruck to Neustift, then on foot or by lift to the Starkenburger Hütte
blurb: A circuit of eight huts high above the Stubai valley: alpine T3–T4 terrain with old snow in early summer, but no glacier travel.
description: A classic hut-to-hut circuit high above the Stubai valley, linking the Starkenburger, Franz-Senn, Neue Regensburger, Dresdner, Sulzenau, Nürnberger, Bremer and Innsbrucker huts in 7–9 days. Expect rocky alpine terrain (SAC T3–T4) with cabled passages and old snow in early summer, glaciers in view but no glacier travel; the high point is the Grawagrubennieder (2,881 m). Huts can be reached from the valley at several points, so it is easy to shorten.

name: Berliner Höhenweg
access: Zillertalbahn to Mayrhofen, bus to Finkenberg
trending_reason: The Zillertal’s classic hut-to-hut route, cresting at 3,134 m
blurb: Eight days hut to hut under the glaciers of the Zillertal main ridge, topping out on the Schönbichler Horn at 3,134 m.
description: Eight days hut to hut through the Zillertal Alps, from Finkenberg to Mayrhofen beneath the glaciers of the main ridge. The route links the Gamshütte, Friesenberghaus, Olpererhütte, Furtschaglhaus, Berliner Hütte, Greizer Hütte and Kasseler Hütte, and tops out on the Schönbichler Horn at 3,134 m. Long, steep stages with cabled sections: for fit, surefooted hikers.

name: Salzburger Almenweg
access: Train to Pfarrwerfen, or start in any Pongau village
trending_reason: A long circuit linking the staffed summer pastures of the Pongau
blurb: A 350 km circuit through the Pongau linking summer pastures and alm huts round the Hochkönig and Tennengebirge.
description: A 350 km circuit in 25 stages through the Pongau, linking the staffed summer pastures around the Hochkönig, the Tennengebirge and the side valleys of the Salzach. Most stages are long but moderate, on farm tracks and alpine paths, with alm huts serving food along the way. Any village in the region makes a starting point, and single stages work as day hikes.
